issues.display_title: Issue #1217: Profile: save the name and avatar to the server (upload, delete)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Counterpart of GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#61 (User Avatar Delete API, PR GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#214). The Profile page's Profile Information card does not talk to the API at all. src/app/profile/profile-client.tsx says so itself (ponytail: avatar / name-save have no server action yet):

  • Upload avatar / Change avatar only shows the picked file in the browser (URL.createObjectURL). Nothing is uploaded, and the picture is gone after a reload.
  • Delete avatar only clears that local preview.
  • Save changes for the name only updates local state. The name is not saved.
  • The card never shows the avatar the profile already has. GET /v1/auth/me returns avatar, but the page ignores it and always starts from initials.
  • The hint "PNG, JPG, WEBP or GIF, up to 4 MB" and accept do not match the API, which takes PNG, JPEG and WebP up to 10 MB.

API

  • POST /v1/auth/update-profile, multipart/form-data: fullname (text) and/or avatar (file part named avatar). Returns user with the new avatar URL. Errors: 400 invalid request (blank name), 400 Unsupported file type, 400 File exceeds 10 MB, 500 Failed to save avatar.
  • DELETE /v1/auth/avatar (new in API-GO#61, needs PR #214 deployed). 200 {message, deleted, user}, where deleted: false means the profile had no avatar. 500 failed to delete avatar image / failed to clear avatar.

Scope

  1. Show the profile's current avatar from me.avatar, with the initials as the fallback.
  2. Upload / Change avatar sends the file through a server action calling update-profile. Show the new avatar on success. Show the API's error message on failure and keep the previous avatar.
  3. Delete avatar calls DELETE /v1/auth/avatar through a server action and goes back to the initials.
  4. Save changes sends fullname through update-profile and keeps the saved name after a reload.
  5. accept and the hint match the API: PNG, JPG, WEBP, up to 10 MB. Refuse a bigger or other file before uploading.
  6. Check how the returned avatar URL loads in the browser. MinIO URLs from the API can point at a LAN host (the project files do: http://192.168.1.12:9199/...), so they may need the existing file proxy and an allowed img-src.

Out of scope

Showing the avatar in other places, such as the dashboard menu or collaborator rows. Cropping or resizing.

Acceptance criteria

  • An uploaded avatar shows on the Profile page and is still there after a reload.
  • Delete avatar removes it, and the initials show after a reload.
  • A saved name is still there after a reload.
  • A GIF or a file over 10 MB is refused with a clear message, and nothing changes.

RESULT

video-1217-profile-name-avatar.mp4

Released to main in 0fe80f5c (release PR #1219). The change came in through PR #1218, merged to development as 6f3fc0e4; the commit is f19a5a49. Deploy succeeded.

The Profile page's Profile Information card now saves to the API. Upload / Change avatar, Delete avatar and Save changes all survive a reload, and the saved avatar shows when the page opens.

Change

  • src/actions/profile.ts (new):
    • updateProfileAction(form) sends fullname / avatar to POST /v1/auth/update-profile.
    • deleteAvatarAction() calls DELETE /v1/auth/avatar (API-GO#61).
    • Failures show the API's own message.
  • Avatar address: on production the API returns a presigned MinIO URL on the bucket's LAN host, which a browser cannot reach.
    • avatarSrc() (src/lib/profile/avatar.ts) maps it, or the API's own path, to /api/avatar/<user>/<file>.
    • The new route src/app/api/avatar/[userId]/[file]/route.ts proxies the API's public avatar endpoint. It sends no credentials and accepts only a UUID plus a plain file name.
  • getMeAction also returns avatar.
  • profile-client.tsx:
    • shows the saved avatar, with the initials as the fallback;
    • upload, change and delete go to the API; on failure the message shows and the old avatar stays;
    • a saved name also updates the account menu;
    • the file is checked first (PNG, JPEG, WebP, up to 10 MB), and the hint and accept match.
  • Not in scope: the avatar in the account menu (still initials).

Tests

  • 22 new tests:
    • address mapping and path safety;
    • the proxy route;
    • the two actions;
    • the Profile card.
  • 19 hand-made mutants: 18 caught. The one survivor showed a redundant decodeURIComponent, which is removed.
  • pnpm test (3005), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real Chrome against a stand-in API that serves avatars as LAN MinIO URLs, as production does, 16/16 (.playwright-mcp/demo/1217/check-profile.mjs):

    • upload, change to a JPG, delete, each after a reload;
    • a GIF is refused;
    • an upload and a delete the API refuses;
    • name save plus the menu, after a reload;
    • no request to the LAN host.

    This covers every acceptance criterion. No real account was written to.

  • Production after the deploy, read only, 8/8 (1217/check-prod.mjs):

    • /profile shows the new hint and accept list, the initials for an account without an avatar, and Save changes disabled until an edit;
    • no page errors and no LAN request;
    • /api/avatar/… answers from the new route: an invalid id gets 404, and an unknown file gets 404 passed through from the API.

  • Not exercised on production: a real upload, delete or rename, which would write to a real account.

  • Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1217/video-1217-profile-name-avatar.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1220: Directions: a door does not open a thick wall, so rooms on large plans stay unreachable ("No route available")
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

On https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N ("Square One Mall V6 (Demo) - copy"), Level 2, directions between FOX and Alo Yoga always end in "No route available". Both rooms have a door.

Cause

Directions run A* on a grid built from the floor's walls (src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts, buildGrid):

  1. Every wall is drawn at its full width.
  2. Each door is then carved back out as a capsule of a fixed 7 px (DOOR_CARVE_R).

That value fits small plans with 8 px walls. On this mall the walls are 27.6 units wide (half-width 13.8). The carve opens only the middle of the wall and leaves both of its faces closed, so a room with a door stays sealed and the route fails.

Measured on the real Level 2 data (GET /v1/live/b9PmEp8N):

  • FOX → Alo Yoga: status none.
  • Grid cells across Alo Yoga's door: open in the middle, blocked on both faces of the wall. FOX's door is the same.
  • Both doors lead into the same open space, so with the walls really opened the two rooms connect.
  • Cutting the walls at the doors with the rule the 2D plan already uses (wallOpenings + openingTolerance, #1211: a wall is cut where a door lies within 0.6 m of its line) finds the route.

Scope

  1. The routing grid cuts walls at doors with the same rule as the 2D plan and the 3D pane: wallOpenings(..., openingTolerance(level)). Only the kept parts of each wall are drawn, so a door opens the whole thickness of the wall it sits on, however thick.
  2. Keep the existing door carve as well, so small plans route as before.
  3. A wall without a door still blocks.

Not in scope (noted)

  • On this project, 324 of the 325 named rooms on Level 2 are wall loops without a door. They stay unreachable until doors are added in the editor.
  • A door placed on a double wall (a second parallel wall about 1 m away) does not cut the second wall. The 2D plan draws it the same way, so the door must sit on the wall it is meant to open.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /v/b9PmEp8N, Level 2, Direction from FOX to Alo Yoga draws a route.
  • A room whose walls have no door is still not entered.
  • Existing routing tests still pass.

RESULT

video-1220-route-through-thick-walls.mp4

Released to main in cd419c58 (release PR #1222). The fix came in through PR #1221, merged to development as 161af368; the fix commit is 5eb49541. Deploy succeeded.

On https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N, Level 2, Direction from FOX to Alo Yoga now draws a route.

Fix

  • buildGrid (src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts) draws only the parts of each wall that no door cuts: wallOpenings(segment, doors, openTol).kept.
    • openTol is the plan's openingTolerance (0.6 m), the rule the 2D plan and the 3D pane use (#1211).
    • A door therefore opens the whole thickness of the wall it sits on, however thick.
  • routePixels (multiLevelRoute.ts) passes openingTolerance(level.floorplanMeta). Without a plan, the old carve radius is the default.
  • The 7 px capsule carve stays, so small plans route as before. The existing bit-identical grid tests pass unchanged.

Tests

  • New src/lib/routing/__tests__/route-thick-walls.test.ts (6 tests) on 27.6-unit walls at 50 mm per unit:
    • two rooms with doors route both ways;
    • a room routes out to the corridor;
    • a room without a door stays closed;
    • a door 10 units off the wall line still cuts it; one 20 units off does not;
    • the default tolerance applies without a plan;
    • the grid cells across the door are open.
  • 13 hand-made mutants are all caught.
  • pnpm test (3009), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real /v/b9PmEp8N payload through planMultiLevelRoute: FOX ↔ Alo Yoga is found both ways. FOX → Gucci stays none, since Gucci has no door.
  • Real Chrome on that payload, A/B 2/2 (.playwright-mcp/demo/1220/check-route.mjs): development shows "No route available", the fix shows "Route found" with 2 steps.
  • Production after the deploy, read only, 1/1: map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N, FOX → Alo Yoga shows "Route found", 2 steps.
  • Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1220/video-1220-route-through-thick-walls.mp4.

Still to do in the editor (not code): the other named rooms on Level 2 have no door yet, so they stay unreachable until doors are added. A door must sit on the wall it opens: one placed on a double wall does not cut the second wall.

issues.display_title: Issue #1223: 3D map: overlapping walls flicker (z-fighting where a Closed room's shell meets another wall)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

In the 3D map, some walls flicker: patches change colour as the camera moves. Two spots on https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N ("Square One Mall V6 (Demo) - copy"):

  1. Level 1, the gap right of Villa Madina, at the corridor edge. A grey patch on top of the walls mixes with pink.
  2. The thin red "Entrance" rooms. Hatching at both ends, where the red shell meets the neighbouring wall.

Cause

canvasDataToGeoJson (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts, 3D mode) builds walls from pieces: a strip per segment and a disc at every joint. Every piece shares the same height (top at the wall height, dark cap 5 cm above it). This import has many overlapping walls. Where two overlapping pieces have different colours, their caps (and touching sides) lie in exactly the same plane, and the GPU alternates between them. That is z-fighting.

Proven with queryRenderedFeatures on the rendered map:

  • Villa Madina gap: a grey corridor wall and its disc overlap Villa Madina's pink wall and disc, both at height 1.5 m.
  • Entrance: the red Entrance walls overlap the walls of the large neighbouring room. That room is also a Closed room, tinted #f5f5f5. So a tinted wall can fight another tinted wall too, not only a plain grey one.

Scope

  1. A Closed room's shell (its strips, and the discs its tint claims) stands slightly above and outside the walls it overlaps, so where two overlap the result is always the same:
    • plain walls stay where they are;
    • Closed-room walls are lifted by 1–4.75 cm (1 cm, plus 2.5 mm per step of room size) and widened by the same amount: the smaller the room, the higher. A small room's shell (an Entrance) shows over a large one's.
  2. The lift stays small enough (under 5 cm) that the wall cap never pokes through the Closed room's roof (10 cm above the wall).
  3. Nothing else changes: heights of plain walls, rooms and areas, door and window openings, room outlines.

Tested beforehand as an experiment on both spots: the flicker is gone and the walls look the same.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /v/b9PmEp8N, Level 1, the gap right of Villa Madina no longer flickers when the camera moves.
  • The Entrance rooms' ends no longer flicker.
  • Plain walls, room roofs and openings look as before.

RESULT

video-1223-wall-zfighting.mp4

Released to main in d83f4686 (release PR #1225). The fix came in through PR #1224, merged to development as 06558b21; the fix commit is 958259aa. Deploy succeeded.

Fix: shellLifts(areas, owners) in src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts.

  • Plain walls stay at the wall height.
  • A Closed room's shell is lifted by 1 cm + 2.5 mm × step, at most 4.75 cm. The step is log2(largest Closed room / this room), capped at 15, so smaller rooms sit higher.
  • Strips take that lift on top, and the same amount outward on their half-width.
  • Joint discs take the lift of the room whose tint they wear, and the lift moves with the tint when a room claims a disc first reached by a plain wall. Disc radius grows by the same amount.
  • The top step keeps the 5 cm cap under the room's roof, which sits 10 cm above the wall.
  • Plain walls, rooms, areas, openings, room outlines and the 2D map are unchanged.

Tests

  • New src/lib/map/__tests__/geojson-shell-lift.test.ts (6 tests):
    • plain walls stay put;
    • shells sit above them, smaller rooms higher;
    • discs follow their tint's lift;
    • the cap stays under the roof;
    • shell strips and discs are slightly wider.
  • 12 hand-made mutants are all caught.
  • pnpm test (3016), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real Chrome (GPU) on /v/b9PmEp8N, development against the fix, 4 frames with the camera nudged:
    • the Villa Madina gap and the Entrance ends are clean on the fix;
    • the wide view is unchanged (0.1 % of pixels differ, all at those spots).
  • Production after the deploy, read only: the same two spots, 4 frames each, are clean.
  • Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1223/video-1223-wall-zfighting.mp4.

Not covered: the editor's own 3D pane (scene3d.ts). Two similar-sized rooms with different colours and overlapping walls can still share a step.

issues.display_title: Issue #1226: Directions: name the room that has no door instead of "No route available"
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

When Direction cannot reach a place because that room has no door, the viewer only says "No route available". Nothing tells the team (or the visitor) what is missing.

Example on https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N, Level 1: Urban Planet → TCX Currency Exchange fails.

  • TCX has a door. Urban Planet has none: none of the floor's 9 doors is on its walls, so the room is sealed.
  • A door on its wall facing the corridor (around x 10108, y 9451) makes the route work (checked with a simulated door).
  • The same happened with FOX and Alo Yoga on Level 2 before they got doors (#1220).

Scope

  1. When a route fails, check whether its start or end is a room the walk cannot leave: from inside the room, no walkable cell outside the room's outline can be reached.
  2. Such a failure names the room: "Urban Planet has no door". When both ends are sealed: "FOX and Alo Yoga have no door".
  3. Every other failure keeps its current message, and so does a room that has a door which leads nowhere useful. The check is conservative: when in doubt, the generic message stays.
  4. It applies to every leg of a trip, and to routes on one floor or across floors of one building.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /v/b9PmEp8N, Level 1, Direction from Urban Planet to TCX Currency Exchange says "Urban Planet has no door".
  • A route that fails for another reason keeps its existing message.
  • Routes that work are unchanged.

RESULT

video-1226-name-sealed-room.mp4

Released to main in c6c8e1af (release PR #1228). The change came in through PR #1227, merged to development as 83e6ebb2; the commit is 7c8afb1e. Deploy succeeded.

On https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N, Level 1, Urban Planet → TCX Currency Exchange now says "Urban Planet has no door".

Change

  • enclosedIn(grid, from, poly) (src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts): a flood on the routing grid from the room's anchor. It answers "shut in" only if no reachable cell lies outside the room's outline.
    • Conservative: a start on no walkable cell answers no.
    • The outline is rasterized once and the buffers are bounded to its bbox: about 60 ms on a 200k-cell shop.
  • planMultiLevelRoute: only after a route has failed, it checks each area end and adds sealed: ["from" | "to"]. This covers same-floor failures and cross-floor failures within one building.
  • buildTrip turns those ends into place names (sealedPlaces).
  • legFailureReason shows "X has no door" or "X and Y have no door". Every other failure keeps its message.

Tests

  • New src/lib/routing/__tests__/route-sealed-room.test.ts (9 tests).
  • Hand-made mutants are all caught (the pin type guard is an equivalent mutant).
  • pnpm test (3026), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real payload: Urban Planet ↔ TCX, and FOX → Gucci ("Gucci has no door"); FOX → Alo Yoga still found.
  • Real Chrome A/B, 4/4: development shows "No route available", the fix shows the room's name.
  • Production after the deploy, read only, 2/2:
    • Urban Planet → TCX shows "Urban Planet has no door";
    • FOX → Alo Yoga shows "Route found".
  • Demo video (.playwright-mcp/demo/1226/video-1226-name-sealed-room.mp4), on a scratch copy since deleted: adding a door to Urban Planet in the editor makes the route to TCX appear.

On the real project: Urban Planet still needs a door on the wall facing the corridor, added in the editor. The live map picks it up without republishing.

issues.display_title: Issue #1229: Directions: cross-floor routes take 10–39 s to fail and don't say the lifts and stairs are walled in
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

On https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N ("Square One Mall V6 (Demo) - copy"), every route between Level 1 and Level 2 fails with "Connector found, but walking route blocked". It fails even between rooms that both have a door, for example FOX (Level 2) → TCX Currency Exchange (Level 1). Each failed attempt also keeps the viewer busy for 10–39 seconds.

Cause

  • Data: all 18 connectors on both floors (Elevator 1–6, Escalator 1–11, Stairs 1) stand inside Closed rooms that have no door: "Elevators", "Escalators", "Stairs", and a few unnamed ones. None can be reached from the corridor, so every cross-floor walk is blocked.
  • The message says a connector exists but not what is in the way.
  • The time: planMultiLevelRoute tries every connector pair that spans the two floors, with a full A* search per leg. A failing search walks the whole reachable corridor before it gives up. With 18 connectors and nothing reachable, that is dozens of full searches on 22-million-cell grids, all in the browser.

Scope

  1. Fail fast. Know which grid cells can reach which (connected areas, computed once per floor and cached). Skip a connector the walk cannot reach before running A* on it. A cross-floor route that cannot work answers in a fraction of the time. A route that can work finds the same path as before.
  2. Name what is in the way. When no connector can be reached on a floor, the message names the rooms the connectors stand in, for example: "The lifts and stairs can't be reached: Elevators, Escalators and Stairs have no door."
    • The rooms of the start and end take precedence, as today (#1226: "X has no door").
  3. Nothing else changes: routes that work, same-floor routes, and other failure messages.

Not in scope

The data itself: the Elevators, Escalators and Stairs rooms on this project still need doors (or the connectors moved into the corridor) before cross-floor routes can work.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /v/b9PmEp8N, FOX (Level 2) → TCX Currency Exchange (Level 1) names the connector rooms instead of "Connector found, but walking route blocked".
  • That route answers in well under the current 10–39 seconds.
  • Cross-floor routes that work return the same path as before.

RESULT

video-1229-walled-connectors.mp4

Released to main in baa35eca (release PR #1231). The fix came in through PR #1230, merged to development as f9786acb; the fix commit is 2065ae67. Deploy succeeded.

On https://map-thru.com/v/b9PmEp8N, FOX (Level 2) → TCX Currency Exchange (Level 1) now answers in 3.5 s (it was about a minute, frozen) with "The lifts and stairs can't be reached: Elevators, Escalators, Stairs and Room 43 have no door".

Change

  • pathfinder.ts:
    • snapIndex is the start cell, now shared with findPath.
    • reachableFrom is one flood from a start, using exactly findPath's moves.
  • multiLevelRoute.ts:
    • One flood from each end; connectors either end cannot reach are dropped before any A* search. A route that can work finds the same path.
    • When a floor has no reachable connector, the route carries blockedConnectorRooms: the named rooms they stand in.
  • trip.ts and TripSummaryCard.tsx: the leg names those rooms, or "… can't be reached from here" when none has a name. The route's own ends (#1226) still come first.

Tests

  • New src/lib/routing/__tests__/route-walled-connectors.test.ts (8 tests), including 0 A* searches when the lifts are walled in, and reachableFrom matching findPath on a corner-only gap.
  • Mutants are all caught.
  • pnpm test (3033), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real payload: 39 s → 2.9 s on the first plan, 0.2 s after that.
  • Real Chrome A/B: development took 59.3 s with the old message; the fix took 3.9 s and named the rooms.
  • Production after the deploy, read only: 3.5 s, with the rooms named.
  • Demo video (.playwright-mcp/demo/1229/video-1229-walled-connectors.mp4), on a scratch copy since deleted: with doors into Escalator 3's room on Level 2 and Level 1, the route appears ("Walk from FOX to Escalator 3 → Take Escalator 3 to Level 1 → Walk to TCX Currency Exchange").

Still to do in the editor (data): the Elevators, Escalators and Stairs rooms on this project need doors on their corridor side before cross-floor routes work there. Escalator 3's room on both floors (around x 9051, y 11011) is enough for one working route.

issues.display_title: Issue #1232: Blue Line Map: thicker tour lines that grow with the zoom, like Google's
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Client feedback: "can we have the Blue Line a bit bigger? how Google has them", with a screenshot of Google Maps' Street View coverage lines.

On MapThru, a Blue Line Map's tour lines are drawn 3 px wide at every zoom (5 px when selected), in #5b8bf7 (src/components/blue-line/map/TourLinesMap.tsx). This applies to the public page /m/{key} and the Blue Line Map editor. Google's coverage lines grow with the zoom: thin when zoomed out, thick on a street.

Scope (MapThru only)

  1. Tour lines grow with the zoom, as Google's do, roughly:

    Zoom 10 13 15 17 19
    Width 1.5 px 3 px 5 px 8 px 12 px

  2. A selected tour stays 2 px wider than the others at every zoom.

  3. The invisible hit area for clicking a line grows with it, so a click on a thick line always lands.

  4. Colours stay as they are: #5b8bf7, and #2563eb when selected.

Not in scope

maps.gothru.co (gothru-maps-frontend) keeps its own line style for now.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /m/{key}, the lines are thin when zoomed out and clearly thicker on a street (about 8 px at zoom 17).
  • A selected line is still wider than the others, in its darker blue.
  • Clicking anywhere on a thick line still selects that tour.
  • The colours are unchanged.

RESULT

video-1232-blue-line-zoom-width.mp4

Released to main in 45609461 (release PR #1235). The change came in through PR #1234, merged to development as 01694d80; the commit is 4f2a5538. Deploy succeeded.

Change (src/components/blue-line/map/TourLinesMap.tsx, used by /m/{key} and the Blue Line Map editor):

  • The line width is exponential by zoom (base 1.6): 1.5 px at 10, 3 at 13, 5 at 15, 8 at 17, 12 at 19.
  • A selected tour is 2 px wider at every zoom.
  • The invisible click target is max(16, width + 10).
  • Colours are unchanged (#5b8bf7, #2563eb selected). maps.gothru.co is not changed.

Tests

  • 4 new tests in TourLinesMap.test.tsx. They evaluate the real paint expressions with MapLibre's createPropertyExpression, covering:
    • the stops;
    • exponential growth between them;
    • the selected tour at +2 px;
    • the click target;
    • the colours.
  • Mutants are all caught.
  • pnpm test (3037), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real Chrome on /m/fPMEbGwq, measured from screenshots: development is 3 px at zoom 14 and at zoom 17; the fix is 4 px and 8 px.
  • Production after the deploy, read only: 4 px at zoom 14, 8 px at zoom 17, and a click 4 px off the line's centre opens the tour.
  • Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1232/video-1232-blue-line-zoom-width.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1236: Editor: doors and windows are sized as if every plan were 50 m across (wall-wide doors, wrong Size readout)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From #1233 (video, Square One Mall V6 (Demo), Level 1).

  • A door added with D covers almost the whole wall it lands on. On a long wall it spans about 20 m, across several shops.
  • Meanwhile the toolbar's Size slider reads 0.90 m, and shrinking the door with the slider barely changes it.

Cause

The editor converts metres to plan units as if every plan were 50 m across (BUILDING_SPAN_M): px = metres × max(w, h) / 50. It ignores the plan's real scale (floorplanMeta.scaleMmPerUnit). Three places use that conversion:

  1. editor/interaction-tools.ts, addOpeningOnWall: a new door or window is 0.9 m × max(w, h) / 50, clamped to 90 % of the wall.
  2. editor/model-sync.ts, setSelectedOpeningWidth: the Size slider sets the width.
  3. editor/model-sync.ts, getSelectedOpeningWidth: the Size slider reads the width.

On Square One (17 204 × 23 014 units, 50 mm per unit):

  • a new door is 414 units = 20.7 m;
  • the slider shows 0.9 m, 23× too small.

This is the same family as #1211 (an opening tolerance taken as 3 % of the plan).

Scope

  1. One conversion between metres and plan units, used by all three places:
    • 1000 / scaleMmPerUnit units per metre when the plan has a scale;
    • otherwise today's max(w, h) / 50, so unscaled plans behave as before.
  2. A new door is 0.9 m and a new window 1.2 m in real size, still clamped to 90 % of a shorter wall.
  3. The Size slider shows and sets real metres, within its 0.3–3 m range.
  4. Doors already drawn keep their size. Once selected, the slider shows their true width and can shrink them.

Acceptance criteria

  • On Square One Mall V6, Level 1, a door added with D is 0.9 m wide (18 units), not wall-wide.
  • The Size slider reads the door's real width, and moving it resizes the door to that many metres.
  • On a plan without a scale, adding and resizing doors works as before.

RESULT

Released to main in ba805575 (PR #1237 → development 12e53669, release PR #1238). The Deploy succeeded.

Cause: the editor converted metres to plan units as if every plan were 50 m across (BUILDING_SPAN_M), ignoring scaleMmPerUnit. On Square One a new door was 414 units = 20.7 m, while the slider read 0.90 m.

Fix (commit adadfb52):

  • New unitsPerMetre(model) in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts: 1000 / scaleMmPerUnit when the plan has a scale, otherwise max(w, h) / 50 (unscaled plans unchanged).
  • Used by addOpeningOnWall (editor/interaction-tools.ts) and by setSelectedOpeningWidth / getSelectedOpeningWidth (editor/model-sync.ts).
  • openingTolerance is now 0.6 × unitsPerMetre(model), with identical values. BUILDING_SPAN_M is removed.
  • Tests: editor/__tests__/opening-width.test.ts (4). All 7 mutants are caught. pnpm test (3041), lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked on scratch copies of Square One Mall V6, Level 1, each deleted afterwards (.playwright-mcp/demo/1236/check-door.mjs):

New door Size slider After +0.5 m
development (before) 414 units = 20.71 m 0.90 m 32.22 m, reads 1.40 m
fix, local 18 units = 0.90 m 0.90 m 28 units = 1.40 m, reads 1.40 m
production (map-thru.com) 18 units = 0.90 m 0.90 m 28 units = 1.40 m, reads 1.40 m

Note: doors already drawn keep their size. The slider shows their true width, and its 0.3–3 m range is unchanged, so a door wider than 3 m shrinks to at most 3 m when the slider is moved.
